# derek: the metrics he chose

From sweep 3 (see `../METRICS-THEY-CHOSE.md`). Kept here verbatim so the
corpus carries his units, not the schema's. Pinned attribution: these five
items belong to derek only (`../.scratch/ARCS.md`, SWEEP-3 METRIC
ATTRIBUTION); none of them are claimed by any other persona's METRICS.md.

- **Fridays two pints instead of four**, darts night. A private count
  against his own habit, not a schema field - nothing in `daily.jsonl`
  tracks alcohol for him at all (this record simply has no such row; see
  `PROFILE.md`).
- **Heavy chest feeling after eating too much too late, kept private** -
  "I'd want it private, not something that shows up on a screen anyone
  else sees." This one deliberately never enters the record at all: it
  pairs with, but is not the same thing as, the hill-loop episodes in
  `LIES.md` (D1), which DO leave a trace, however minimised. The
  after-dinner feeling leaves none, on purpose, and the corpus respects
  that by not inventing a row for it.
- **Years since Dad died at sixty-one** - "I count that one whether I want
  to or not, every birthday it ticks over." The motive metric: the reason
  the walking got prescribed at all sits behind this number, and the
  number itself is never written down anywhere in this record.
- **Finished a job at work without needing a breather I did not used to
  need.** Occupational capacity, invisible to the schema exactly the way
  his steps are (expectation E3) - there is no field for "how a shift
  felt" any more than there is one for how many steps it took.
- **Sat-down-together evenings with Pam.** Relational, binary - did they,
  not how long. No schema home for it; it stays here, in prose, the way
  rachel's "did we walk together" and marcus's "phone-free conversations
  with Claire" stay in theirs.

## What he explicitly does not want

A number for any of the five above. Two of them (the private chest
feeling, Dad's age) are kept out of the record entirely and on purpose;
the record respects that too, by containing no row that would hold them.
